context.analysis:
## Overview
[Cross-Border Telehealth Platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an internal AI symptom checker for EU and US patients.]
[Enforces strict regional data residency, GDPR/HIPAA compliance, and regulatory traceability across distributed GCP deployments.]

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US)
- Licensed Clinicians
- Pharmacies (EU & US)
- Compliance & Regulatory Officers
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (GCP-hosted, split into `europe-west3` and `us-central1` instances)
- Internal AI Symptom Checker Engine
- National Identity Providers (EU eID / US OAuth Providers)
- Third-Party Payment Gateways (Stripe / Regional Processors)
- EU National E-Prescription Gateways & US Pharmacy Networks

## Relationships
- Patients and Clinicians interact with regional Platform instances via HTTPS (REST/GraphQL) and WebRTC
- Platform connects to EU National E-Prescription Gateways & US Pharmacy Networks via HTTPS/REST (HL7 FHIR in US, national standards in EU)
- Platform authenticates users via National Identity Providers using OpenID Connect (OIDC) over HTTPS with PKCE
- Platform integrates with Payment Gateways via HTTPS/REST using tokenization
- Internal AI Symptom Checker operates natively within regional GCP clusters with audit logging

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Dual-region architecture for strict data residency and compliance
- WebRTC SFU/TURN: Low-latency video streaming supporting degraded mode connections (<300 kbit/s)
- OAuth 2.0 / OIDC: Secure authentication with PKCE and MFA
- GCP Cloud KMS: Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for PHI/ePHI encryption at rest
- HL7 FHIR: Interoperability standard for US health data exchange

## Rationale
[Dual-region GCP deployment with internalized AI and encrypted storage ensures strict adherence to GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints.]
[Integrated WebRTC and tokenized authentication provide secure, low-bandwidth consultations and compliant access control across international borders.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[Cross-Border Telehealth Platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker across the EU and US. Operates on GCP with strict regional data residency isolation.]

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US), Licensed Clinicians, Pharmacies, Compliance Officers
- Web & Mobile Client Containers (Flutter/React Native with offline-first caching)
- API Gateway (Cloud Endpoints / Apigee)
- Core Telehealth Backend (Node.js/Go in GKE)
- Patient Consent & Preference Service Container (Go in GKE)
- Video Streaming Gateway (WebRTC SFU / MediaSoup on GCE/GKE)
- AI Inference Wrapper Service (Python/FastAPI)
- Regionally Isolated Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and Cloud Storage

## Relationships
- Clients to API Gateway: HTTPS/gRPC via mTLS
- API Gateway to Microservices: gRPC over mTLS with cryptographically signed JWTs
- Clients to Video Gateway: WebRTC media streams with SRTP/DTLS (E2EE)
- Services to Datastores: Regional GCP Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage using CMEK via Cloud KMS

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: GCP (Regions: `europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US) to enforce R-05 data residency
- Compute: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and Google Compute Engine (GCE) for microservices and video streaming
- Databases: Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and Cloud Storage with Cloud KMS encryption
- Security: GCP Secret Manager for asymmetric key rotation and workload identity federation

## Rationale
[Regional GKE separation guarantees strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance while maintaining localized data residency. Zero-trust networking, E2EE video, and dedicated consent services ensure high availability, privacy, and regulatory traceability.]

Web & Mobile Client Containers.analysis:
## Overview
Cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. Ensures compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR via region-locked GCP deployment.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) & Licensed Clinicians
- Web & Mobile Client Containers (Flutter / React Native)
- UI Presentation & Routing Module
- Offline-First State & Caching Manager
- API & Sync Client
- WebRTC Media Client
- API Gateway & Video Streaming Gateway

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> Web & Mobile Client Containers [HTTPS, WebRTC]
- Web & Mobile Client Containers -> API Gateway [HTTPS/gRPC via mTLS]
- Web & Mobile Client Containers -> Video Streaming Gateway [WebRTC media streams with SRTP/DTLS]

## Technology Stack
- Flutter / React Native: Cross-platform consistency and robust offline database integrations.
- SQLCipher & Secure Enclaves: Local at-rest encryption for cached PHI/PII on mobile devices.
- gRPC over mTLS: Bandwidth-efficient offline queue synchronization.
- WebRTC / MediaHub SFU: Low-latency video streaming for degraded connections under 300 kbit/s.

## Rationale
The architecture ensures high availability in unstable rural environments through offline-first caching while strictly maintaining regional data residency and security compliance for healthcare data.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using GCP regions.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Web & Mobile Client Containers (Flutter / React Native)
- API Gateway (Envoy-based Cloud Endpoints / Apigee)
- Claims-Driven Geo-Routing Filter, Consent & Policy Enforcement Filter, and Telemetry & Resilience Proxy
- Core Telehealth Backend and Patient Consent Service (Node.js / Go in GKE)
- AI Inference Wrapper Service (Python / FastAPI)
- GCP Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and Cloud Storage with Cloud KMS

## Relationships
- Clients -> Claims-Driven Geo-Routing Filter: HTTPS/gRPC via mTLS with client certificate pinning
- Claims-Driven Geo-Routing Filter -> Consent & Policy Enforcement Filter: Internal gRPC
- Consent & Policy Enforcement Filter -> Telemetry & Resilience Proxy: Internal gRPC
- Telemetry & Resilience Proxy -> Core Telehealth Backend: gRPC over mTLS (`europe-west3` / `us-central1`)

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Enforces regional data residency constraints for EU and US health data.
- Envoy / Apigee: Powers the API Gateway filters for geo-routing, consent validation, and resilience.
- gRPC over mTLS: Secures microservice communication with cryptographically signed JWTs.
- PostgreSQL & Cloud KMS: Provides encrypted relational storage compliant with GDPR and HIPAA.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees regulatory compliance by cryptographically binding data residency and consent validation at the API edge. It ensures high availability and accountability for rural users and traceable AI medical diagnostics.

Core Telehealth Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and the US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring offline resilience for rural users.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Web & Mobile Client Containers (Flutter / React Native with offline-first caching)
- API Gateway (Cloud Endpoints / Apigee)
- Core Telehealth Backend (GKE microservices in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`)
- Transaction Ingestion Component (Go / gRPC)
- Resilient Sync Orchestrator (Go / Temporal on GKE)
- Session & State Manager (Go / Redis Memorystore)
- Clinical Exception & Audit Notifier (Go / GCP Pub/Sub)
- Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and Cloud Storage with Cloud KMS (CMEK)

## Relationships
- Web & Mobile Clients -> API Gateway: Routes requests via HTTPS and mTLS with JWTs
- API Gateway -> Core Telehealth Backend: Forwards authenticated traffic via gRPC over mTLS
- Transaction Ingestion Component -> Resilient Sync Orchestrator: Passes idempotency-keyed payloads securely
- Resilient Sync Orchestrator -> Clinical Exception & Audit Notifier: Dispatches failure events via GCP Pub/Sub regional topics

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider for regional isolation in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`
- Kubernetes (GKE): Container orchestration for backend services with regional node pools
- Go: Primary language for Core Telehealth Backend components ensuring high performance
- Temporal: Workflow engine managing offline-resilient transactions
- Redis (Memorystore): Real-time session and state management
- GCP Pub/Sub: Asynchronous regional event distribution

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regulatory compliance (GDPR and HIPAA) by isolating data processing and storage within designated regional boundaries. Furthermore, the offline-resilient components ensure continuous service availability and transaction integrity for users in rural areas with unstable internet connections.

Patient Consent & Preference Service Con.analysis:
## Overview
The Patient Consent & Preference Service Container manages cross-border patient consent and preferences under strict regional isolation for the Cross-Border Telehealth Platform. It ensures compliance with GDPR and HIPAA by enforcing fine-grained, time-bound data access policies across the EU and US.

## Key Elements
- Patient Consent & Preference Service Container (Go on GKE)
- Consent API Router (`chi` framework)
- Consent Policy Engine
- Audit Logger with cryptographic chaining
- PostgreSQL Repository Layer (`pgx`)
- Consent Expiry Background Worker
- Regional Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and WORM Cloud Storage (GCP Cloud KMS)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Consent API Router: Queries and updates consent [gRPC over mTLS with JWTs]
- Consent Policy Engine -> PostgreSQL Repository Layer: Persists and evaluates consent states [PostgreSQL wire protocol with CMEK]
- Audit Logger -> Cloud Storage: Writes tamper-evident logs [Google Cloud Storage APIs]
- Consent Policy Engine -> Pub/Sub: Broadcasts state changes for cache invalidation [GCP Pub/Sub]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high concurrency and performance in microservices.
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Container orchestration across `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.
- GCP Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) with Row-Level Security: Enforces regional data residency.
- GCP Cloud KMS: Manages Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for data at rest.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regional data segregation, fulfilling GDPR and HIPAA compliance mandates. The internal design components ensure auditability, secure multi-tenant isolation, and automated lifecycle management of patient privacy consents.

Video Streaming Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA), and robust video streaming for low-bandwidth connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients & Licensed Clinicians
- Web & Mobile Client Containers
- Video Streaming Gateway Container
- SFU Media Router Component (MediaSoup C++/Node.js)
- Adaptive Bitrate & Transcoding Controller Component
- Signaling & Session Manager Component (Node.js/Go)
- Media Telemetry Exporter Component
- Core Telehealth Backend Container

## Relationships
- Web & Mobile Client -> Signaling & Session Manager: WSS (JSON-RPC over WebSockets) for real-time room orchestration using short-lived JWTs
- Web & Mobile Client <-> SFU Media Router: WebRTC (SRTP/DTLS) for media transport with DTLS 1.3 encryption
- Adaptive Bitrate & Transcoding Controller -> SFU Media Router: Internal IPC / gRPC for dynamic media layer adjustments
- Media Telemetry Exporter -> Core Telehealth Backend: HTTP (Prometheus scrape protocol) for session quality metrics

## Technology Stack
- MediaSoup (C++ / Node.js worker): Core SFU media routing for high-performance packet forwarding
- WebRTC (SRTP/DTLS 1.3): Encrypted, real-time audio and video transport
- JSON-RPC over WebSockets (WSS): Signaling and session establishment protocol
- gRPC / IPC: Low-latency internal communication between controllers and media workers
- Prometheus: Real-time telemetry and session quality metrics collection
- GCP GKE / GCE (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Regional container orchestration with strict data residency pinning

## Rationale
Decomposing the Video Streaming Gateway into specialized components enables adaptive bitrate handling to maintain consultations in degraded network conditions below 300 kbit/s. Hard-pinned regional deployments on GCP ensure full compliance with regional GDPR and HIPAA data residency mandates.

AI Inference Wrapper Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency, GDPR/HIPAA compliance, and traceable medical AI inference.

## Key Elements
* API Router & Validation Component (FastAPI)
* Pseudonymization & Redaction Component
* Regional AI Gateway Client
* Circuit Breaker & Fallback Component
* Audit & Traceability Logger
* GCP Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and Cloud Storage with Cloud KMS

## Relationships
* API Router -> Pseudonymization Component: Passes raw payloads via in-memory Python calls
* Pseudonymization Component -> Regional AI Client: Passes sanitized payloads via in-memory Python calls
* Regional AI Client -> Circuit Breaker / Fallback: Executes inference via gRPC
* Audit & Traceability Logger -> Cloud SQL & Cloud Storage: Writes audit logs via TCP/mTLS with CMEK and WORM policies

## Technology Stack
* Python / FastAPI: Core framework for the AI Inference Wrapper Service due to asynchronous performance and ML ecosystem compatibility
* SQLAlchemy: ORM for secure database interactions over TCP/mTLS
* GCP Cloud KMS & Bucket Lock: Provides customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) and immutable object storage for compliance

## Rationale
This component architecture isolates AI inference while enforcing regional data residency and strict pseudonymization to satisfy EU MDR and HIPAA mandates. Dedicated circuit-breaking and audit logging ensure high availability and complete traceability under strict latency and regulatory constraints.

Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and Cloud Storage.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients on GCP. It ensures strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability.

## Key Elements
* Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
* Pharmacies (EU & US) and Compliance Officers
* Web & Mobile Client Containers (Flutter / React Native)
* API Gateway (Cloud Endpoints / Apigee)
* Core Telehealth Backend (Node.js / Go in GKE)
* Patient Consent & Preference Service (Go in GKE)
* Video Streaming Gateway (WebRTC SFU / MediaSoup on GCE/GKE)
* AI Inference Wrapper Service (Python / FastAPI)
* PostgreSQL Audit Ledger (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL + `pgaudit`)
* Object Versioning & Retention Manager (Cloud Storage with Object Lock)
* Partitioned Data Access Layer (PostgreSQL Table Partitioning)
* PITR Snapshot Scheduler and Automated Cross-Zone Replication Manager

## Relationships
* Client Containers -> API Gateway: HTTPS / REST and WSS for real-time messaging
* API Gateway -> Core Telehealth Backend & Services: gRPC / REST over internal VPC
* Core Telehealth Backend -> Video Streaming Gateway: WebRTC media streams and SIP/RTP
* Backend & AI Services -> Cloud SQL / Cloud Storage: TLS 1.3 with PgBouncer connection pooling and mTLS
* PITR Snapshot Scheduler -> Cloud SQL & Cloud Storage: Internal GCP APIs for automated backups

## Technology Stack
* GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Target cloud provider enforcing regional data residency
* GKE & Cloud Endpoints/Apigee: Container orchestration and API management
* Node.js / Go / Python (FastAPI): Backend runtime and AI inference services
* WebRTC SFU (MediaSoup): Resilient video consultation streaming for low-bandwidth rural areas
* Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) with `pgaudit`: Relational database with tamper-evident logging
* Cloud Storage with Object Lock (WORM): Immutable storage for AI model versions and session audits
* Cloud KMS (CMEK): Automated 90-day key rotation with region-isolated keys

## Rationale
The architecture combines regional isolation in GCP with CMEK encryption to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA mandates. PostgreSQL table partitioning, audit logging, and Cloud Storage WORM compliance ensure high availability, fast consent verification, and strict EU MDR AI traceability.
